case_reviews.mathematics: Bound(c) iff Z and r≤c and (c=0 implies H) holds for all extended coefficients. For finite existence, c=r+1 is finite positive when r<∞, so H is not needed. Any least finite coefficient c must equal r: if r<c, choose r<b<c, which is finite positive and feasible, contradiction. Hence the exact attainment criterion includes r=0 implies H.
case_reviews.lean_semantics: ratioSup indexes actual points with d≠0 and d≠∞; ENNReal.div_le_iff applies precisely there. bound_iff splits zero, infinity and finite-positive source values, including zero_mul at c=0. LeastFinite explicitly quantifies over every finite feasible competitor. least_coefficient_eq derives the value rather than storing it in a hypothesis. boundary_ratio, boundary_feasible and boundary_not_attained use concrete Unit functions d=∞ and e=1.
boundary_checks: Empty X gives vacuous Z,H, r=0 and minimum 0.
A zero source with nonzero target violates Z and disallows every coefficient.
Finite positive source with target infinity forces r=infinity and excludes finite feasibility.
At infinity source, every positive coefficient gives infinity but coefficient zero gives zero; thus H matters only for r=0 attainment.
No attainment of the pointwise ratio supremum is assumed or required.
